title: Zero polynomial verifier specification
statement: Let $x$ be a finite Boolean string, and let $L$ be the language of Boolean strings encoding well-formed arithmetic circuits over the integers whose output polynomial is identically zero. On a uniformly random Boolean string $r$ of length $2400(|x|+1)^2$, the verifier accepts with probability at least $2/3$ if $x\notin L$; if $x\in L$, it rejects for every such $r$.
hypotheses_covered: If $x\notin L$, the acceptance probability is at least $2/3$ over uniformly random strings of length $2400(|x|+1)^2$
If $x\in L$, the verifier rejects on every Boolean string of that length
caveat: The statement depends on a particular circuit encoding and verifier construction; the prose describes their mathematical role but not the encoding details.
